subject: Order Form: service guarantee reconciliation and next steps
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@avenuecloud.com>

Cc: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@avenuecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: AVENUE - Order Form v3 + SLA redlines

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. Attached is our redline set for the order form (AvenueCloud_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf) — legal marked up a few SLA items we need clarified before we can sign:

- Uptime target: they inserted 99.99% for the hosted API; we understand you typically list 99.95%. Need rationale and whether credits scale.
- Service credits: they proposed a flat 10% credit for any month below target; we'd prefer a tiered credit schedule tied to minutes of downtime.
- Response windows: P1 initial response within 30 minutes and remediation within 4 hours.
- Maintenance windows: customer notice window of 7 days and no scheduled work during our peak period (Mon-Thu 08:00-18:00 PT).
- Data retention & audit evidence: they asked for audit log retention and SOC2 evidence (we can follow up separately).

We'd like to reconcile these items this week and get to a counter-signature by the 20th. Can you confirm who on your side will handle legal redlines and operational commitments? Also attaching the marked-up PDF.

Appreciate it — Sanjay

--
Sanjay Rao
Head of Procurement, AvenueCloud
sanjay@avenuecloud.com
(415) 555-0198
From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AVENUE - Order Form v3 + SLA redlines

Sanjay — thanks for the redlines and the clear priorities. I want to propose a short process to avoid back-and-forth and hit your sign-by date:

1) We (Redwood) will produce a consolidated counter-redline that keeps your key protections but aligns to our operating model. Expect that file by EOD tomorrow. (attachment: redwood_sla_response_draft.docx)
2) We will call out the non-negotiables vs. negotiables so your legal team can triage quickly.
3) Ops walkthrough with your SREs to confirm maintenance windows and runbook expectations prior to signature.

Quick preview of the items we'll address in the counter:
- Uptime: propose 99.95% for hosted API, with a tiered credit table (0.5% credit per 0.1% below target up to a cap). We can escalate to 99.99% only for Dedicated commitments (reserved capacity) where throughput isolation is guaranteed.
- Credits: a tiered monthly credit schedule rather than a single flat percent. Credits apply to the invoice for the affected month only.
- Response times: P1 initial acknowledgement within 1 hour and a target remedy window of 8 hours for hosted; faster SLAs possible under Dedicated.
- Maintenance: standard weekly maintenance window of up to 4 hours, 72-hour notice for scheduled work; emergency maintenance communicated ASAP and not counted as downtime if for security patches where we can provide evidence.

If this approach works, I'll loop in Laura for commercial terms and Aditya for operational details. Can we schedule a 30-min alignment call Thursday?

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

Subject: Re: AVENUE - Order Form v3 + SLA redlines

Sanjay / team — looping in Operations (Hannah) and our contracts lead (Dev) to make sure we capture downstream impacts. A few commercial points up front: 

- We cannot commit to 99.99% on hosted without Dedicated capacity — that level requires capacity isolation and is tied to a committed monthly minimum. If AvenueCloud is interested in Dedicated terms, we can provide a separate addendum with an elevated uptime and different credits.
- On credits: we'll send a proposed tiered schedule. To reduce billing churn, credits apply as invoice adjustments and do not convert to refunds.
- Response SLAs: 30-min initial P1 ack is aggressive for hosted; 1 hour is our standard for P1 on hosted. We are willing to include an escalations path and named contacts for P0/P1 incidents.
- Maintenance windows: we can accommodate a blackout for your stated peak hours for scheduled maintenance, but that will reduce our available maintenance capacity. We will need a signed mutually agreed maintenance calendar for the first 90 days post-go-live.

I will attach a short commercial note and the proposed credit matrix after Priyom shares the counter. Also flagged to Dev for a quick legal redline on liability/force majeure carve-outs.

- Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: AVENUE - Order Form v3 + SLA redlines

Folks — quick technical notes to include in the counter so AvenueCloud understands operational tradeoffs: 

- Maintenance window specifics: our standard approach is rolling maintenance across clusters to avoid full-customer outage. We can reserve a weekly 4-hour window (non-overlapping with your peak) during which we perform routine OS/kernel patching and model container refreshes. If you require full-stack maintenance suppression for certain days, we can do that but it requires increased monitoring and a maintenance bank (approved exceptions).
- Failover behavior: transient performance regressions due to autoscaling or model fallback (e.g., switching to a lower latency model variant to preserve availability) will be classified as degraded performance rather than downtime. We should include clear metric definitions in the SLA (how we measure availability — API 5xx, token generation timeouts, queue length).
- Incident evidence: we'll commit to providing timeline exports (incident start/end), call recordings from our war room on request, and diagnostic logs for agreed-upon time window (we should define retention in the order form).

I'll add two bullets to the draft: one that defines availability measurement (metric names & thresholds), and another that defines the credit computation table. That should remove a lot of ambiguity.

-aditya

--
Aditya Rao

Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: AVENUE - Order Form v3 + SLA redlines — Redwood counter and next steps

Sanjay / Maya — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is Redwood's consolidated counter (Redwood_CounterOrderForm_20280412_redlines.pdf). High level summary of changes and asks: 

1) Uptime / credits
- Hosted availability: 99.95% monthly uptime target.
- Credit table (monthly invoice adjustment):
  * >= 99.95%: 0% credit
  * 99.90% - 99.95%: 2% credit
  * 99.80% - 99.90%: 5% credit
  * < 99.80%: 10% credit (cap)
- 99.99% option: available as a separate Dedicated addendum with minimum committed spend.

2) Response / remediation
- P1: initial acknowledgement within 1 hour, status updates every 60 minutes until remediation plan in place. Target remediation window for hosted: 8 hours (varies by incident class).
- P2: acknowledgment within 4 hours, remediation target 24 hours.

3) Maintenance
- Standard weekly maintenance up to 4 hours; 72-hour notice for planned work.
- Blackout/peak protections: we will honor a customer-specified blackout for up to 10 business days per year if scheduled at contract signing; otherwise we propose a mutually agreed 90-day calendar post-go-live.

4) Metrics & evidence
- Availability measured by API 5xx rate and hard token-generation timeouts; definition table in section 3.
- Redwood will provide rolling 90-day diagnostic logs and post-incident report templates.

Next steps we propose:
- 30-min ops/contract call Thursday 4/13 to walk the counter and confirm the maintenance calendar.
- If the counter is acceptable, we will generate a DocuSign envelope (link in related_links) and route to legal for final signature.

Please review the attached counter and flag any absolute blockers. If you'd like a different credits cadence (e.g., per-minute instead of monthly buckets), call that out and we can evaluate.

Looking forward to closing this out — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
